findings.title: Null-strategy test parameterization does not actually test the 'feature disabled' path; it relies on the feature being baked into the custom image
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns early for the null (default) strategy without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature in the Keycloak CR, which reads as if the default-strategy tests exercise the operator without the feature. However, the same PR modifies operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image to run `kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`, so the feature is enabled inside the image the tests deploy regardless of the CR. This means the documented behavior in docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc ("While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail") is never actually tested: there is no test where the feature is genuinely absent and the operator's failure mode is asserted. In particular testCacheMaxCount with the null strategy expects eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus, which only works because the operator's compatibility check succeeds against the image-baked feature. A real user deploying a stock image without the feature would hit the documented failure, which no test covers. Either the parameterization should explicitly enable/disable the feature in the CR for both strategies, or a negative test for the feature-disabled failure should be added.

findings.title: No test asserts the new exit code 4 (feature disabled), the documented scripting contract
findings.body: The PR introduces exit code 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) and documents it in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc as the contract for CI/CD scripts ("Exit Code 4: Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled."). However, testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message text via cliResult.assertError(...); it never asserts that the process actually exits with code 4. Since the whole point of the exit-code table is to be relied upon by automation, and the check command's feature-disabled path is not tested at all (only the metadata command is), a regression that returns a different exit code would go unnoticed. Add exit-code assertions (e.g., assertEquals(4, result.exitCode())) and a test for the check subcommand with the feature disabled.

findings.title: Exit code 4 description is inaccurate for the metadata subcommand
findings.body: The exit-code table describes exit code 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." That description only makes sense for the `check` subcommand. The `metadata` subcommand (update-compatibility metadata) also exits with code 4 when the feature is disabled (UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()), but in that case no rolling-upgrade evaluation happened and no metadata was produced — it is simply a command failure. Script authors handling both subcommands with one exit-code table will misinterpret a code 4 from `metadata` as an incompatibility verdict rather than 'the command did not run'. The table should state that exit code 4 means the command was not executed because the feature is disabled.
